notes: September 2026 cycle. Japan bot traffic (adjustment code `j`), MIDDLE scenario, plateau 67,101 DAU/day = 6.19% of Japan. Population is defined by a four-clause behavioural conjunction (hours=under-1min, uri=0-2/3-10, is_default=false, age=0-6d/7-27d) which contains NO channel term -- ESR is an outcome (95.1% of the flagged population) rather than an input, so the finding is not circular. Baseline is flat at 1,876 +/- 265 DAU/day across 2025-01-01..2026-05-15, so the component is a subtraction and not a fitted residual; an independent construction (ESR channel minus a fitted pre-onset trend) agrees to 2.3%. Onset detected 2026-06-24. Curve is measured raw daily excess through 2026-08-30, then an arrival-rate projection convolved with a measured per-cohort kernel (4.94 active days per profile for projected arrivals), held flat to 2027-12-31 -- NOT zero-filled, which would drop the component on 2027-01-01. History is DELIBERATELY UNSMOOTHED: the daily swing is real contamination, not measurement error, so a smoothed subtraction would leave a synthetic oscillation in the training frame. Allocation is 100% Japan, fixed. modern_windows by measurement (99.2% Windows_NT, 97% NT 10.0, 78% build 26200). NO DOUBLE-COUNT with `o`: the flagged population is 95.1% ESR and the MozillaOnline migration is entirely non-ESR (zh x ESR moved -23 DAU/day year on year); `o` already allocates 0.98% of its curve to JP and that is a different population. NOT WIRED: main.py hand-wires each overlay code, so `j` needs a _find_japan_bot_spec_for_forecast / _apply_japan_bot_pre_mozaic pair plus an add_lift_to_forecast call, and a registry entry in adjustment_codes.yaml. Two-letter codes are NOT available -- parse_state_from_path splits the marker into characters. Producer: scratch/brwells/regional-story/forecast, evidence page site/forecast.html.
